awardBodies.name: CAMRA Pub Design Awards (run jointly with Historic England)
awardBodies.note: VERIFIED LIVE 13 Sep 2026, found via a Secret London syndication trail (see editorialLists) rather than search. Judged by a panel of design and conservation experts across five categories: Conversion To Pub Use, Historic England Award for Conservation, New Build Award, Refurbishment Award, and The Community Local Award. This is a GENUINELY DIFFERENT CAMRA programme from the London-branch Pub of the Year already collected for data/topics/craft-beer-pubs.json - that one (london.camra.org.uk and its 13 branch sub-sites) judges beer and pub-going quality per branch; this one (camra.org.uk/awards/pub-design) judges architecture and design, UK-wide, with no branch structure. No URL overlap - not a trap-13 duplicate. NATIONAL, NOT LONDON-ONLY (trap 12) - every year's winners must be scoped to London venues before counting, and non-London winners (Liverpool, Marlow, Birmingham, Lichfield, Farnham, Kington, Gorsedd, North Walsham all appeared across the two years checked) must be excluded the way the Good Food Guide's bakeries list should have been. Two years read in full: 2026 named 5 London-area results - Blue Stoops, Kensington (Conversion To Pub Use, joint winner with a Liverpool pub); Leyton Engineer, Leyton (Refurbishment, winner); European, Leyton (Refurbishment, Highly Commended); Duke of York, Fitzrovia (Refurbishment, Commended); Lord Southampton, Kentish Town (Community Local, winner). 2025 named only 1 London result - Forester, West Ealing (Community Local, winner). Yield is real but thin and swings year to year, the same shape as CAMRA's branch POTY data - budget for reading several years back, not just the current one, when real collection starts. IMPORTANT: this award is the strongest evidence found this pass that 'beautiful' and 'historic' are genuinely different questions in London pubs specifically - Blue Stoops is a 2020s conversion of a former wine bar with no historic pedigree at all, and a New Build Award category exists for brand-new pubs. None of the five 2026 London winners, and the one 2025 winner, appear anywhere in src/content/articles/historic-pubs-dining-rooms-london.md.

specialistBlogs.name: Boak & Bailey
specialistBlogs.note: VERIFIED real, live and directly relevant - the strongest single find for the 'pub-architecture or Victoriana blog' lead the brief asked for. Jessica Boak and Ray Bailey are named, published beer historians (Brew Britannia; the award-winning 20th Century Pub, 2017; blogging independently since 2007) - a genuine single-subject specialist, the same standing this project already gave Will Hawkes on data/consensus/craft-beer-pubs.json. Domain is NOT currently in data/sources.json - will default to tier C with a warning per the registry's own rule, which matches the tier used here. Has a dedicated tag archive at boakandbailey.com/tag/pub-design/, read in full: 'The Champion, Fitzrovia: a Victorian fantasy' (2020) is a well-sourced piece establishing that the pub's 'Victorian' etched glass, mirrors and mahogany are actually a documented 1954 Festival-of-Britain-era design job by architects Sylvia and John Reid, done for Barclay Perkins, and that the room visitors see today is a LATER re-pastiche of even that - 'much of what evokes The Olden Days in British pubs is rarely more than 30 years old.' The Champion does not appear anywhere in src/content/articles/historic-pubs-dining-rooms-london.md - a real, well-evidenced, beauty-not-history venue this topic could use honestly that the existing historic guide could not (a manufactured Victorian look is a liability under a 'how old is this really' frame and a non-issue under a 'is this beautiful' one). Two further posts on the same tag are pub-design-adjacent but not venue-specific ('Why are horse brasses a pub thing?', 'The traditional pub bar is pretty annoying and badly designed') - background reading, not sources.

openVenueQuestions: THE CENTRAL QUESTION FOR THIS TOPIC - ASK ROB BEFORE COLLECTING, per the task brief's explicit instruction to flag rather than silently proceed if research keeps surfacing the historic-pubs guide's own venues. src/content/articles/historic-pubs-dining-rooms-london.md already has a section, 'The listed interiors', explicitly organised around beauty rather than age - its own words: 'Age is the wrong measure for several of London's best pubs. These are protected for what is inside them.' Of the nine pubs in that section, THREE are near-certain re-crowns under any beauty-focused research that uses CAMRA's own interior-rating language, because the existing guide already uses exactly that language for them: The Blackfriar ('the finest surviving Arts and Crafts pub interior in Britain'), The Guinea ('an interior CAMRA rates three-star - of outstanding national historic importance') and The Viaduct Tavern ('one of the best-surviving Victorian gin palaces in London'). A further three - The George Southwark, The Seven Stars and Ye Olde Mitre - are looser candidates, cited there mainly for rarity, food or folklore rather than decor, that a beauty guide might or might not re-pull depending on framing. Against that, this pass found real, DIFFERENT material the historic framing structurally cannot claim: CAMRA's Pub Design Awards winners (Blue Stoops, Leyton Engineer, European Leyton, Duke of York Fitzrovia, Lord Southampton - all recent design or conversion work with no old-pedigree angle), plus Boak & Bailey's The Champion, Fitzrovia (looks Victorian, is documented 1950s pastiche - a venue whose manufactured history is a liability under a 'how old is this really' frame and irrelevant under a 'is this beautiful' one). So the honest answer is a REAL BUT PARTIAL differentiation, not a clean yes or no. Three options for Rob: (a) build the guide anyway, accept that 3-6 headline venues will likely be shared with historic-pubs as ordinary cross-topic overlap - the project already does this elsewhere (Blacklock, Hawksmoor etc. recur across several food topics) - and lead with the new-build/design-award material as the actual point of difference; (b) fold this idea into historic-pubs-dining-rooms-london.md instead, expanding its existing 'listed interiors' section, given SKILL.md's own rule that pages targeting the same search intent compete and both rank worse; (c) sharpen the angle further before collecting at all - e.g. restrict explicitly to JUDGED DESIGN OR RESTORATION WORK (the CAMRA Pub Design Awards' actual remit) rather than a general 'prettiest pubs' framing, which is the version of this topic with the least overlap risk but also the thinnest source pool found so far (one award body, annual, single-figure London yield most years).
